literal: Prince Zhen of Beiping, styled Renjian, was the fifth son of Wucheng.
idiomatic: Prince Zhen of Beiping, styled Renjian, was the fifth son of Gao Zhan.

literal: Deeply thoughtful and magnanimous in pardon.
idiomatic: He was composed in judgment and generous in forgiveness.

literal: The emperor often said: "This boy has my phoenix down.
idiomatic: The emperor often said, "This boy has inherited my finest plumage.

literal: " He held in succession the ranks of Governor of Si Province, Grand Commander of the Capital Region, and concurrently Chief Minister of the Masters of Writing and Recorder of Affairs of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: " He held in succession the governorship of Si Province, grand command of the capital region, and the concurrent posts of chief minister and recorder of affairs of the Masters of Writing.

literal: When the emperor went on tour, he was left in overall charge of affairs at the capital.
idiomatic: When the emperor traveled, he was left in overall charge of the capital.

literal: Over the years, as Zhen grew to maturity, the Later Lord came gradually to be wary of him.
idiomatic: Over the years, as Zhen came of age, the Later Lord grew wary of him.

literal: Anaogong, reading the emperor's intent, had Feng Shigan impeach and imprison Zhen, stripping him of his authority as regent in the capital.
idiomatic: Anaogong, reading the emperor's intent, had Feng Shigan impeach Zhen and imprison him, stripping him of his authority as regent in the capital.

literal: Prince Renying of Gaoping was the sixth son of Wucheng.
idiomatic: Prince Renying of Gaoping was the sixth son of Gao Zhan.

literal: His bearing was lofty and dignified; his spirit was unfettered by restraint.
idiomatic: His bearing was lofty and dignified, his spirit unbound by constraint.

literal: He held the post of Governor of Ding Province.
idiomatic: He served as Governor of Ding Province.

literal: Prince Renguang of Huainan was the seventh son of Wucheng.
idiomatic: Prince Renguang of Huainan was the seventh son of Gao Zhan.

literal: He was by nature impulsive and violent; he held the post of Magistrate of Qingdu.
idiomatic: He was impulsive and violent by nature and served as Magistrate of Qingdu.

literal: Next came Prince Renji of Xihe, who from birth lacked firm bone and could not support himself;
idiomatic: Next came Prince Renji of Xihe, born without firm bone, unable to support himself;

literal: next, Prince Renyong of Leping;
idiomatic: next, Prince Renyong of Leping;

literal: next, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan;
idiomatic: next, Prince Renjian of Yingchuan;

literal: next, Prince Renya of Anle, who had been mute from childhood;
idiomatic: next, Prince Renya of Anle, mute from childhood;

literal: next, Prince Renzhi of Danyang;
idiomatic: next, Prince Renzhi of Danyang;

literal: and last, Prince Renqian of Donghai.
idiomatic: and last, Prince Renqian of Donghai.

literal: All were raised in the Northern Palace.
idiomatic: All were raised in the Northern Palace.

literal: After the Prince of Langya died, the restrictions on the princes grew ever stricter.
idiomatic: After the Prince of Langya died, the princes were kept under ever tighter guard.

literal: In the closing years of Wuping, Renyong and those below him were at last allowed to go outside; their provisions were miserly, barely enough to subsist.
idiomatic: In the closing years of Wuping, Renyong and those below him were at last allowed outside; their provisions were meager, barely enough to live on.

literal: Before long, with the Later Lord hard pressed, Kuo was assigned Guang Province, Zhen Qing Province, Renying Ji Province, Renjian Jiao Province, and Renzhi was made Governor of Ji Province.
idiomatic: Before long, with the Later Lord hard pressed, Kuo was sent to Guang Province, Zhen to Qing Province, Renying to Ji Province, Renjian to Jiao Province, and Renzhi was made Governor of Ji Province.

literal: From Kuo downward, most died at Chang'an together with the Later Lord.
idiomatic: From Kuo downward, most died at Chang'an with the Later Lord.

literal: Renying was spared on account of his pure madness; Renya on account of his muteness; both were exiled to Shu.
idiomatic: Renying was spared for his innocent eccentricity, Renya for his muteness; both were exiled to Shu.

literal: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, Renying was summoned back; an edict ordered him, together with Xiao Cong and Chen Shubao, to restore the sacrificial rites of their ancestral houses.
idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era of Sui, Renying was recalled; an edict ordered him, with Xiao Cong and Chen Shubao, to restore the sacrificial rites of their ancestral houses.

literal: Before long he died.
idiomatic: Before long he died.

literal: The Later Lord had five sons: Empress Mu bore the Young Lord; various consorts bore Prince Ke of Dongping, then Shande, then Maide, then Zhiqian.
idiomatic: The Later Lord had five sons: Empress Mu bore the Young Lord; various consorts bore Prince Ke of Dongping, then Shande, then Maide, then Zhiqian.

literal: Empress Dowager Hu had Ke succeed to the line of the Prince of Langya; he soon died young.
idiomatic: Empress Dowager Hu had Ke succeed to the Prince of Langya's line; he soon died young.

literal: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou brought to Chang'an some thirty princes great and small from the Prince of Rencheng downward, all granting them ranks and fiefs.
idiomatic: When Qi fell, Emperor Wu of Zhou brought to Chang'an some thirty princes great and small from the Prince of Rencheng downward, all granting them ranks and fiefs.

literal: Afterward those who had not been executed were scattered to the western frontier, all dying on the borders.
idiomatic: Afterward those spared execution were scattered to the western frontier, all dying on the borders.

literal: Discussion: The sons of Wenxiang all possessed striking presence; though in the way of cultured elegance they fell short of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, yet in martial skill and heroic bearing many were fit to repel insult.
idiomatic: Discussion: Gao Cheng's sons all had striking presence; though in cultured elegance they fell short of the Duke of Zhou and Duke of Shao, in martial skill and heroic bearing many were fit to repel insult.

literal: Even if swords were granted at Xianyang, signs of overturn were already there; had the Prince of Lanling been preserved whole, what might have been cannot be measured — and yet in the end they were cut down one after another, until the state collapsed in ruin. A matter for deepest sighing indeed.
idiomatic: Even if swords were granted at Xianyang, signs of ruin were already plain; had the Prince of Lanling been preserved whole, what might have been cannot be measured — yet in the end they were cut down one after another until the state collapsed. A matter for deepest sighing.

literal: Ande, finding the times perilous and the ruler benighted, hid his tracks and kept his light under a bushel; yet at the battle of Pingyang he summoned his loyal valor — for facing peril in crisis, his devotion to house and state ran deep.
idiomatic: Yanzong of Ande, finding the times perilous and the ruler benighted, hid his tracks and kept his light under a bushel; yet at the battle of Pingyang he summoned his loyal valor — for facing peril in crisis, his devotion to house and state ran deep.

literal: When Dezhi launched his great action, affairs pressed the feelings of the multitude; the logic led to extinction, with nowhere left to turn for deliverance.
idiomatic: When Dezhi launched his great action, affairs pressed the feelings of the multitude; the logic led to extinction, with nowhere left to turn for deliverance.

literal: Guangning's request to leave the inner palace was never fulfilled — not that Xiaoxheng's words lacked the persuasiveness of Li Tong; from that time the Later Lord's heart and mind had already drifted far from Pingyuan.
idiomatic: Guangning's request to leave the inner palace was never granted — not that Xiaoxheng's words lacked the persuasiveness of Li Tong; from that time the Later Lord's heart and mind had already drifted far from Pingyuan.

literal: The matters of survival and destruction differ — how can they be spoken of in the same breath?
idiomatic: Survival and destruction are not the same matter — how can they be spoken of in one breath?

literal: Wucheng was cruel, licentious, and corrupt — his conduct pushed the bounds of human relations.
idiomatic: Gao Zhan was cruel, licentious, and corrupt — his conduct pushed the bounds of human relations.

literal: Taiyuan's conduct seemed strange and bred suspicion; in sentiment there was no rebellion, yet disaster arose from Zhaoxin, and thus came excessive punishments.
idiomatic: Shaode of Taiyuan's conduct seemed strange and bred suspicion; in sentiment there was no rebellion, yet disaster arose from Empress Zhaoxin, and thus came excessive punishments.

literal: Alas!
idiomatic: Alas!

literal: To seek long endurance — never yet has such a thing been seen.
idiomatic: To seek long endurance — never yet has such a thing been seen.

literal: One might have hoped that Xiaozhao's virtuous reputation could bring blessing down upon later generations, but a century of cruelty — perhaps Jinan was the headwater whence it all flowed.
idiomatic: One might have hoped that Xiaozhao's virtuous reputation could bring blessing down upon later generations, but a century of cruelty — perhaps Jinan was the headwater whence it all flowed.

literal: His words, 'Do not imitate your predecessors' — how they stir one's grief! That each man loves his own son — can it really be so?
idiomatic: His words, "Do not imitate your predecessors" — how they stir one's grief! That each man loves his own son — can it really be so?

literal: The Prince of Langya, though without tutors' instruction, had early shown noble character.
idiomatic: The Prince of Langya, though without tutors' instruction, had early shown noble character.

literal: He Shikai's licentious misrule had endured for many years; in a single morning it was cut down, and joy filled court and countryside — that for this he should meet his death is deeply painful.
idiomatic: He Shikai's licentious misrule had endured for many years; in a single morning it was cut down, and joy filled court and countryside — that for this he should meet his death is deeply painful.

literal: Yet the offense of unauthorized killing could not be entirely set aside; to posthumously grant him the imperial title and the epithet Gong — to straighten the crooked went too far. To discern benevolence through one's faults — is this not different from that principle?
idiomatic: Yet the offense of unauthorized killing could not be entirely set aside; to posthumously grant him the imperial title and the epithet Gong — to straighten the crooked went too far. To discern benevolence through one's faults — is this not different from that principle?

literal: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
idiomatic: The entire text has been collated against the November 1972 first edition of the Book of Northern Qi published by Zhonghua Shuju.
